summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with fibrosing mesenteritis, recurrent small bowel obstruction, and chronic pain, was admitted for worsening abdominal pain and acute chest pain. Imaging confirmed a partial small bowel obstruction due to strictures from mesenteric fibrosis and post-pyloric migration of her G-tube. She was managed conservatively with NPO status, IV fluids, pain control, and G-tube replacement for proper decompression. TPN was initiated due to persistent high G-tube output and inability to maintain oral intake. Octreotide was started to reduce secretions, which led to decreased output and improvement in symptoms. Her chest pain, ruled out for cardiac cause, was attributed to abdominal distension. Leukopenia resolved spontaneously, and levothyroxine was adjusted for a suppressed TSH. Warfarin dosing was modified due to vitamin K in TPN. She was transitioned to a low-fat diet, discontinued TPN, and discharged home on octreotide with follow-up planned.
